summary: Evidence is direct for explicit planner-executor separation and adjacent for strong-versus-weak model economics. It remains limited for the exact claim that a larger planner with a smaller executor, or the reverse, is consistently better than a single model under matched cost.

items.text: Plan-and-Act: Improving Planning of Agents for Long-Horizon Tasks — Lutfi Eren Erdogan et al. (2025). The framework trains a planner to emit structured high-level plans and an executor to translate them into actions, reaching a reported 54% success rate on WebArena-Lite. This directly supports role separation, but it does not isolate model size as the causal factor.

Plan-Then-Execute: An Empirical Study of User Trust and Team Performance When Using LLM Agents As A Daily Assistant — Gaole He, Gianluca Demartini, and Ujwal Gadiraju (2025). A CHI study with 248 participants across six tasks found that high-quality plans and appropriate user involvement can help, while plausible faulty plans can miscalibrate trust. This supports inspectable plans and checkpoints, not a particular two-model size split.

RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs from Preference Data — Isaac Ong et al. (2025). ICLR evaluations report more than a twofold cost reduction without quality loss on selected public benchmarks by routing between stronger and weaker models. This is adjacent economic evidence; query routing is not the same as assigning complementary planner and executor roles.
